nativeConstraint.summary: The picture is a native scrcpy child window reparented into the Electron window with SetParent, not a DOM video element.
consequences: The child paints above every web-rendered pixel and cannot be overlapped by HTML controls.
The stage must remain a plain rectangle; radius and hairline are removed in fill-window and fullscreen.
Stage geometry is reported through ResizeObserver and scaled by devicePixelRatio before the child is positioned.
No required control, tooltip, or status may sit over the stage while the child is embedded.
Exit from immersive modes relies on Esc (when the app window holds focus), Ctrl+Alt+W, and Ctrl+Alt+F; the persistent status icon stays in the toolbar.

layout.windowDefault: 1380×860 max, or work area minus 60px, centered
layout.immersive: Toolbar and remote hidden; main padding/gap 0; stage border and radius 0.

accessibility: Layout checked at Windows 150% display scaling.
Focus-visible is a 2px orange outline with 2px offset on buttons; the IP field uses an orange border plus a 3px orange-alpha ring.
Pin, remote, window-fill, and fullscreen toggles expose aria-pressed.
prefers-reduced-motion reduces animation and transition durations to 0.01ms.
Every remote action has a keyboard path: app-level arrows/Enter/Backspace when the UI holds focus; scrcpy keys when the picture holds focus.

evidence.verdict: Ship for the one scored material fix (power pill neutralized; red only on :active). Not a re-certification of the whole surface.
evidence.note: The BrowserWindow pre-paint #0e0e10 is a native anti-flash value, not a palette surface token.

narrative.overview:
A desktop Apple TV console, not a scrcpy shell. One dark, quiet window holds the TV picture as the hero and a physical-feeling clickpad remote beside it. The world is built from tvOS dark materials: a near-black ground, translucent charcoal cards, 1px seams, and system orange as the only accent. It deliberately refuses the old top-bar-plus-button-grid dashboard and any generic mirroring-tool chrome.

The composition is one glance: the stage takes every remaining pixel, and the 280px remote is the only permanent control column. The primary action lives inside the stage's connect card, never in the toolbar. Failure returns that same identity card with the exact cause and a focused retry. The remote stays visually neutral until ADB is healthy; connection health is the only place green, amber, and red appear.

Materials are glass without gloss: 24–30px blur at 160% saturation, long soft shadows, and no decorative gradients except the clickpad's physical shading. Motion is short and mechanical: 140ms for state, 80ms for press, a 1.2s status pulse. The macOS traffic lights are a deliberate Apple-world signature, not a Windows chrome default.
keyCharacteristics: Picture-first: a pure-black stage with charcoal glass chrome.
One accent: system orange; green/amber/red reserved for connection health and the active stop.
One family: SF-style system sans at a fixed 12/13/14/15/22 ramp, weights 510/590.
Physical centerpiece: a 184px circular clickpad with four direction zones and a 64px OK.
Quiet remote: neutral icon+label pills; power red only while pressed; the active stop is red.
Native-aware: the embedded scrcpy child owns the stage; no required web overlay in immersive modes.
Calm by default, exact on failure: status icon, error banner, focused retry.
Bilingual: every visible string switches between 中文 and English in place; connection and error copy are localized from state codes.
Settings hides the native scrcpy child while open, so the sheet stays fully visible over the stage.
Power is never a setting: every press opens the confirmation popover; only the confirm sends KEYCODE_POWER.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Orange is the only accent hue. Green, amber, and red are connection-health signals, the power-pill press state, and the active stop, never decoration or secondary branding.

rules.name: The Black Stage Rule
rules.body: Pure black belongs to the picture stage; the recessed IP field is a black wash at 35%. The window ground is #1c1c1e, and no raised chrome surface is black.

rules.name: The Power-Neutral Rule
rules.body: The power pill is neutral at rest. Red appears only while it is held (:active), never as a resting color.

rules.name: The Calm Remote Rule
rules.body: Remote controls stay neutral at rest; only white-alpha fills respond to hover and press. The toolbar may show active orange; the remote may not, except the power press.

rules.name: The Fixed Ramp Rule
rules.body: Type sizes come only from 12 / 13 / 14 / 15 / 22px. Create hierarchy with weight (510/590), color (label versus secondary), and spacing, never with a new size.

rules.name: The System-Sans Rule
rules.body: The system sans is the identity. Do not introduce a display, serif, or mono face; use tabular numerals for addresses.

rules.name: The Native-Child Rule
rules.body: The picture is a native scrcpy child window reparented with SetParent, not a DOM video element. It paints above every web-rendered pixel and receives the stage's CSS rectangle scaled by devicePixelRatio. The stage must therefore remain a plain rectangle whose only web decoration is a 1px hairline and a 16px radius while the child is inset; fill-window and fullscreen remove both. Never place a required control, tooltip, or status over the stage when the child is embedded; exit relies on Esc (when the app window holds focus), Ctrl+Alt+W, and Ctrl+Alt+F, and the persistent state capsule lives in the toolbar.

rules.name: The One-Glance Rule
rules.body: Picture and controls share one window. The primary action lives in the stage's connect card, never in the toolbar; the toolbar holds only status, mode, and window controls.

rules.name: The Long Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are large-blur and low-contrast under floating panels and the clickpad. No hard offsets, no neobrutalist edges, no stacked shadow sets.

rules.name: The Material-Only Gradient Rule
rules.body: The only gradient in the system is the clickpad's radial charcoal shading (`circle at 50% 30%`, #3a3a3c → #2c2c2e → #242426). Never use gradients as decorative background washes.

rules.name: The Circle Rule
rules.body: Circles mean an object you press or a status indicator. Panels and fields stay rectangular with continuous corners; do not turn cards into capsules.

dos: Do keep the window ground (#1c1c1e) and the picture black (#000000) separate; black is the stage's material, not the chrome's.
Do use system orange (#ff9f0a) as the only accent, and reserve green/amber/red for connection health plus the held power pill's red press and the enabled disconnect stop.
Do build surfaces from rgba(44,44,46,.72) over 24–30px blur with saturate(160%) and a 1px rgba(255,255,255,.10) hairline.
Do keep the connect card at 460px max with a 44px input and a 44px full-width orange action in the stage.
Do keep the clickpad 184px with 44px direction zones, a 64px OK, and 8px edge insets.
Do keep remote pills neutral at rest and use only white-alpha hover and press fills.
Do preserve the focus contract: a 2px orange outline with a 2px offset on buttons, and an orange border plus 3px ring on the IP field.
Do honor the native child: no required web control over the stage in fill-window or fullscreen; exits stay on Esc and the global shortcuts.
Do route every visible string through i18n.js; do hide the native child while the settings sheet is open.
donts: Don't add a second accent hue or tint the remote card orange; orange is a signal, not a wash.
Don't put red on the power pill at rest; red appears only while it is held. Don't show the stop red while it is disabled.
Don't use decorative gradients; the clickpad's radial material is the only permitted gradient.
Don't use hard offset shadows, neobrutalist borders, or glossy bevels; shadows are long, soft, and low-contrast.
Don't introduce type sizes outside 12/13/14/15/22 or a non-system display face.
Don't use emoji, glyph characters, icon fonts, or raster icons; draw inline SVG on the 16px grid.
Don't place labels, tooltips, or controls above the embedded picture in immersive modes; the native child will cover them.
Don't turn cards into capsules or squares; panels use 22px, the stage 16px, controls 8–10px, and circles are reserved for physical or indicator objects.
